name: Rubrik, Inc.

profile.description: Rubrik provides cloud data security and cyber resilience solutions, including enterprise data protection, data threat analytics, security posture management, identity recovery, and cyber recovery. The AI-powered platform (Ruby AI agent, SentryAI) helps organizations detect, respond to, and recover from cyberattacks. Founded in 2013 by CEO Bipul Sinha, IPO'd April 2024, with $1.57B subscription ARR and 2,805 customers with $100K+ ARR. Gartner Magic Quadrant Leader for Backup and Data Protection for 7th consecutive year.

innovation.label: STRONG
innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): Rubrik disrupted the legacy backup market dominated by Dell EMC, Veritas, and Commvault by building a cloud-native, immutable architecture from scratch, then pivoted to position as a cybersecurity company — delivering 48% revenue growth in FY2026 to $1.32B and reaching first GAAP profitability in Q1 FY2027 ($0.16 EPS, beating consensus of -$0.11 by 245%) [1][4]. Subscription ARR reached $1.57B (+32% YoY) with Q1 FY2027 revenue of $387.1M (+39%) [4]. AI Deployment (2/2): Rubrik ships multiple AI-powered products — Ruby, a natural language AI agent for cyber resilience; SentryAI for deep learning-based system health monitoring; anomaly detection and threat hunting capabilities; and Identity Resilience for securing enterprise identity landscapes [2]. These are shipping products generating measurable customer value in a market where AI-powered attacks demand AI-powered defense. Market Share (1/2): Gartner Magic Quadrant Leader for Backup and Data Protection for 7th consecutive year, with 2,805 customers at $100K+ ARR (up 25% YoY) including PepsiCo, GSK, Home Depot, and Allstate [1]. Competes against Veeam, Cohesity-Veritas, and Commvault without dominant market share. Product Pipeline (2/2): Identity security product growing rapidly within the platform; FY2027 guidance targets $1.83B ARR and $265-275M free cash flow with specific quarterly milestones; Q2 FY2027 guided to $345-365M revenue [1][4]. R&D Intensity (1/1): Heavy R&D investment with $329.4M in stock-based compensation (FY2026) funding engineering talent, well above industry average for infrastructure software [1].

inspiration.label: DEVELOPING
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (3/4): Rubrik's mission to 'secure the world's data' is specific, thoughtful, and connects the company's work to a genuine societal need — protecting organizations from the escalating ransomware and cyberattack epidemic [2]. CEO Bipul Sinha consistently articulates this mission, stating Rubrik's job is 'not to fall in love with our own technology, but to fall in love with customers' challenges.' The mission has guided strategic decisions including the pivot from backup to cyber resilience and recruitment of former CIA CISO Michael Mestrovich and ex-Palo Alto Networks CEO Mark McLaughlin to the board [2]. Community Impact (1/2): Rubrik's 'Beyond Work' CSR program pledges company resources to community benefit, and the company's core product directly protects hospitals, schools, and critical infrastructure from cyberattacks [3]. However, specific dollar amounts and measurable impact data for charitable programs are not publicly disclosed. Employee Retention (0/2): R.A.D.I.C.A.L. values emphasize autonomy, transparency, and innovation, and Sinha promotes diversity of thinking. However, no specific employee turnover or tenure data was found for the 3,797-person company [2]. Insider Buying (0/2): No evidence of meaningful net insider buying in the last 12 months. As a recently IPO'd company (April 2024), insiders may still be in lock-up expiration selling mode [4].

infrastructure.label: DEVELOPING
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored on available metrics. Revenue growth of 45.7% TTM is exceptional, scoring perfectly [1][4]. Revenue growth 5yr CAGR of approximately 45% (estimated from pre-IPO revenue trajectory through $1.42B TTM) also scores perfectly with 2x weight [4]. However, Forward P/E of 282.95 (reflecting $83.64 stock price against thin expected GAAP earnings) scores 0 as it far exceeds the 60 floor. Profit margin of -20.3% TTM scores 0, though this is improving — Q1 FY2027 achieved first GAAP profitability at $0.16 EPS [4]. D/E and ROE are excluded (data unavailable for recently IPO'd company with accumulated losses). FY2027 guidance targets non-GAAP EPS of $0.07-0.27 and FCF of $265-275M, demonstrating path to sustained profitability [1]. Cash and investments of $1.68B against $1.13B convertible notes provides net-cash-positive balance sheet [1]. Liquidity floor cleared: 3.03M avg volume x $83.64 = $253.4M daily [5].

ai_resilience.label: LOW RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (8/9): Rubrik is structurally immune to AI disruption — the company IS part of the AI defense infrastructure. As CEO Sinha articulates, AI weaponization by nation-state actors and ransomware groups creates an asymmetric threat that makes data security platforms MORE essential, not less [2]. AI increases the attack surface exponentially ('you cannot bring a human-speed solution to an agent-speed attack'), driving demand for Rubrik's automated cyber resilience capabilities. No analyst cites AI as a substitution risk for Rubrik; the consensus is that AI is a secular tailwind for cybersecurity spending. The company's 2,805 enterprise customers with deep integrations create high switching costs [1][2]. AI Opportunity (1/1): Rubrik generates meaningful AI revenue through Ruby (natural language AI agent for cyber resilience), SentryAI (deep learning health monitoring), Identity Resilience, and ML-based threat analytics — all shipping products embedded in the platform that customers pay for as part of the $1.57B subscription ARR [1][2][4].

infinite_game.summary: Rubrik under Bipul Sinha shows strong infinite game characteristics — the company was founded with a long-term vision of data security before ransomware was a mainstream concern, and Sinha has consistently invested in platform capabilities over short-term profitability for an entire decade. The willingness to remain unprofitable while building a $1.57B ARR platform, then reaching GAAP profitability in Q1 FY2027, demonstrates patience and conviction. Recruiting elite talent (former CIA CISO, ex-Palo Alto Networks CEO) signals institution-building. However, at 13 years old, the company has not yet been tested through multi-decade challenges or leadership transitions.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (2/3): Rubrik's mission to 'secure the world's data' is genuine, specific, and increasingly validated by the ransomware epidemic that makes data protection a critical societal need [2]. Sinha founded the company before ransomware was mainstream, and the mission has guided consistent strategic decisions — the pivot from backup to cyber resilience, the expansion into identity security, and the recruitment of former CIA CISO Michael Mestrovich all trace back to the cause. However, at 13 years old, the cause hasn't been tested through decades of execution or leadership transitions.

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): Rubrik's R.A.D.I.C.A.L. values emphasize autonomy, transparency, and direct communication [2]. Sinha promotes diversity of thinking and has learned over time that 'strength comes from diversity of thinking and approaches.' He openly acknowledged that early delegation to hired executives caused departmental tensions and sluggish decision-making, requiring a management restructuring — suggesting trust-building has been a genuine learning process rather than an inherited strength. Recruiting world-class board members (former CIA CISO, ex-Palo Alto CEO) signals commitment to elite talent [2].

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (1/1): Sinha frames AI-powered attackers as worthy rivals whose escalating capabilities force Rubrik to continuously improve its defensive platform — framing the cybersecurity challenge as an infinite game where the goal is to stay ahead rather than 'win' [2]. His philosophy of 'not falling in love with our own technology, but with customers' challenges' reflects a learning orientation focused on improvement rather than competitive destruction.

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): Rubrik pivoted from backup and recovery infrastructure to a cybersecurity and cyber resilience platform, and more recently expanded into identity security as a growing product line [1]. These represent meaningful strategic evolution within an adjacent domain, driven by the mission of securing data rather than desperation. However, these are incremental adaptations within the data security ecosystem, not a transformative reinvention of the company's core identity.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (2/2): Sinha demonstrated extraordinary courage by founding Rubrik to disrupt the entrenched backup market dominated by Dell EMC and Veritas, choosing to remain unprofitable for a full decade while building a $1.57B ARR platform [1][2]. He rebuilt the management structure when delegation wasn't working, replacing biweekly 30-minute meetings with weekly 3-hour working sessions. The decision to invest heavily in AI security capabilities (Ruby, SentryAI, Identity Resilience) while still pre-profit shows long-term conviction over short-term earnings optimization. IPO'd in April 2024 during uncertain markets, and the company reached GAAP profitability in Q1 FY2027 — validating a decade of patient investment [4].

investment_thesis: Rubrik delivered a blowout Q1 FY2027 with $387.1M revenue (+39% YoY), GAAP EPS of $0.16 (beating -$0.11 consensus by 245%), and subscription ARR of $1.57B (+32% YoY) — achieving first-ever GAAP profitability [4]. The company raised all FY2027 guided metrics: $1.83B ARR, $1.6B revenue, non-GAAP EPS of $0.07-0.27, and $265-275M FCF [1][4]. Operating cash flow margin of 21% and free cash flow margin of 19% demonstrate operating leverage emerging in the model [4]. Rubrik's position as Gartner MQ Leader for 7th consecutive year, 2,805 customers with $100K+ ARR, and AI-powered cyber resilience platform (Ruby, SentryAI, Identity Resilience) position it in a secular growth market where AI-driven cyberattacks drive non-discretionary enterprise spending. Net-cash-positive balance sheet ($1.68B cash vs. $1.13B convertible notes) and board talent (former CIA CISO, ex-Palo Alto Networks CEO) signal institution-building [1][2].
thesis_continued: The bear case centers on extreme valuation and growth deceleration risk. At forward P/E of 282.95 and $17.22B market cap, the stock prices in sustained hyper-growth — any deceleration below 30% revenue growth could trigger severe multiple compression [5]. Revenue growth already decelerated from 48% (FY2026) to 39% (Q1 FY2027), and FY2027 guidance implies ~21% full-year growth, suggesting a meaningful step-down [1][4]. The company remains GAAP unprofitable on a trailing basis (-20.3% profit margin) due to $329.4M in annual stock-based compensation that inflates non-GAAP metrics [1]. A February 2026 log server breach — while contained and transparently handled — is reputationally damaging for a cybersecurity company and follows a 2023 breach from the Clop/GoAnywhere attacks [3]. Competition from Veeam, Cohesity-Veritas, and Commvault remains intense, with each investing heavily in AI and cloud capabilities. As a recently IPO'd company, insider lock-up expirations create potential selling pressure.
key_catalysts: FY2027 ARR target of $1.83B with $265-275M FCF and first-ever GAAP profitability trajectory could trigger institutional re-rating as Rubrik transitions from growth to profitable growth [1][4]
AI-driven cyberattack escalation creates secular demand tailwind — as nation-state actors weaponize AI, enterprise spending on cyber resilience platforms like Rubrik becomes non-discretionary [2]
Identity Resilience and expanded AI security product suite (Ruby, SentryAI) create multiple growth vectors within existing customer base of 2,805 enterprises with $100K+ ARR [1][2]
key_risks: Revenue growth deceleration from 48% (FY2026) to guided ~21% (FY2027) at a forward P/E of 282.95 creates severe valuation compression risk — any further slowdown could trigger a significant stock re-rating [4][5]

Competitive intensity — Veeam, Cohesity-Veritas, and Commvault are investing heavily in AI-powered data security, creating pricing pressure and feature parity risk in a market where switching costs exist but are not insurmountable [1]
February 2026 log server breach and 2023 Clop/GoAnywhere breach represent reputational risk for a cybersecurity company, even though both were contained and disclosed transparently [3]
